context: Paper 4 body upload to Grammarly Coda editor through HASHI Browser Bridge
symptom: One approved 10,126-word paste rendered a duplicated paragraph sequence even though the browser workflow performed only one intended paste.
cause: The editor/browser interaction produced multiple rendered block sequences; the exact mechanism was not isolated.
detection: Direct editor-row reconstruction found 201 non-empty rows instead of 101 and repeated paragraph occurrences.
recovery: Do not detect or edit. Preserve evidence, repair only the new Grammarly document if safe, then verify paragraph count, unique occurrences, first/last fingerprints, canonical text hash, and reload state before continuing.

symptom: The displayed word counter appeared plausible while the editor contained duplicated or otherwise anomalous rendered text.
cause: The counter did not expose the editor's actual paragraph multiplicity reliably enough for integrity validation.
detection: Word-count display disagreed with reconstructed rows and unique paragraph occurrence checks.
recovery: Use the counter only as supporting evidence; require full text reconstruction, canonical hash, paragraph order/count, first/last fingerprints, and duplicate checks.

symptom: A title fill reached an off-canvas duplicate control while the visible document retained an automatic title.
cause: Multiple title-like controls existed and a selector did not prove which one was visible.
detection: Visible screenshot/title and recorded intended title disagreed.
recovery: Target the visible control only and verify the rendered title after editing; do not treat a successful fill call as proof.

context: Replacing one Paper 4 paragraph in the Grammarly Coda editor
symptom: The typing helper collapsed a verified programmatic selection and inserted the candidate at a later stale caret while the target paragraph remained unchanged.
cause: Programmatic DOM selection and the browser input helper did not share a stable editing focus/range.
detection: Word count rose, the target text was unchanged, and the candidate appeared at an unintended location.
recovery: Use one bounded undo only when its effect is provable, verify exact restoration, and stop. Never trust programmatic selection plus typing on real text without a disposable preflight.

symptom: Native Ctrl+A selected only one paragraph rather than the complete batch editor.
cause: The editor uses block-level contenteditable behaviour in which the first selection command is scoped to the active block.
detection: Visible selection and unchanged remaining paragraphs showed that the whole editor was not selected.
recovery: Do not delete or replace. Prove a complete-editor selection method on a disposable multi-paragraph document and validate the entire replacement by hash before production use.

symptom: Creating a separate R1 document avoided unsafe replacement but changed the document-level experimental context.
cause: The same-document replacement path had not been validated.
detection: R0 and proposed R1 had different document identities even though the batch boundaries were intended to match.
recovery: Prefer a preflight-proven same-document whole-batch replacement. Use paired documents only after an explicit run amendment and label target attribution as potentially confounded.

context: Paper 4 whole-body and 927-word Batch 001 Grammarly baselines
symptom: The same opening material participated in a 75% whole-body result and an 87% batch-only result, while issue ordering/severity for the first 18 findings remained reproducible.
cause: Detector percentage depends on submitted context and review-unit boundaries.
detection: Frozen whole-body and bounded-batch records used different text hashes and word counts.
recovery: Compare only identical ordered batch contexts across rounds; never aggregate batches or compare a batch percentage directly with a whole-document percentage.

symptom: Locally extracted Notes were initially treated as a proposed separate Grammarly document without a demonstrated need or separate upload authority.
cause: Local preservation/mapping was incorrectly conflated with external review scope.
detection: User challenged why Notes needed upload before any Notes content was sent.
recovery: Treat local extraction as preservation only. Require a positive unit-level allowlist and explicit approval; notes, footnotes, and endnotes remain local by default.

symptom: The run began traversing 135 findings and captured 19 explanations before proving that one correction-and-recheck loop could be executed safely.
cause: Evidence collection scaled ahead of end-to-end control validation.
detection: User paused the harvest and redirected the task to a bounded proof of concept.
recovery: Prove the complete loop on one bounded batch first; expand only after browser replacement, target outcome capture, and Word checkpoint validators pass.

context: Paper 4 Grammarly run after pivot to Batch 001
symptom: Top-level run_summary.md and rewrite_ledger.md described an earlier state while later batch artefacts recorded an R0 baseline and six prepared R1 candidates.
cause: Run artefacts were updated independently without a mandatory checkpoint reconciliation transaction.
detection: Cross-file review found inconsistent active state, allowlist description, and candidate count.
recovery: At every checkpoint reconcile summary, manifest, allowlist, browser session, attempt ledger, round records, and evidence paths before forward work. Append an amendment; do not erase historical records or repeat external requests.
